source.title: Two gluing methods for string C-group representations of the symmetric groups

principal_boundary: Theorem1.1, the supporting Lemmas3.1–3.2 and4.2–4.6/4.9, all positive Proposition4.7/4.10 families, and complete uniform Proposition4.8 disproof. Ancillary exclusions and two retained classical inputs are separately visible below.

records.result: Literal pure-leaf gluing, with the first label order reversed; all subset intersections.
records.proof: Accepted core common-point theorem + pure-leaf saturation; application §1
records.qualification: Pure endpoint mark is essential. No claim for a distinguished edge carrying additional transpositions.

records.result: Supported symmetric group on the bridge component, independent of the complementary induced group; transitive case symmetric.
records.proof: Accepted core pure-bridge lemma and its restriction-cancellation proof; application §1

records.result: Pure leaf attachment preserves C; connected old/new graphs yield symmetric groups.
records.proof: Accepted core common-point theorem, leaf case; application §1

records.result: All adjacent-path simplex markings, r≥1.
records.proof: Parallel common §2 diagonal case and edge-transposition generation

records.result: Any disjoint union of identically labelled rank-r simplex paths, r≥1.
records.proof: Parallel common §2, identical-copy diagonal argument

records.result: Aligned simplex paths on r+1 and h+1 vertices, r≥2,1≤h≤r−1, yield S_(r+1)×S_(h+1) with IP.
records.proof: Parallel Theorem2, path with connected terminal deleted set; §6 exact adapter
records.qualification: Source attributes result to Fernandes–Leemans–Mixer2012 Lemma6.1; no priority claim.

records.result: Folded path gives C2 wr S_r, r≥2, full marked IP.
records.proof: Parallel Theorem4 and its endpoint path specialization

records.result: Auxiliary two-component family gives S_(r+2)×S_r and C-marking for every r≥3.
records.proof: Application Lemma2, explicit group generation/dihedral boundary/end induction
records.qualification: Retains source Proposition2.2 endpoint central extension and Proposition2.3 criterion, exactly attributed; removes source [6,Theorem2] classification of first-row action.

records.result: Same family at r=2 is D8, not S4×S2.
records.proof: Application Lemma2, product order four
records.qualification: This is the source’s own boundary remark, not an added claimed source result.

records.result: For all r≥3 and1≤h≤r−2, folded path with pure tail is string C of S_(r+h+1).
records.proof: Application Lemma1 and following exact h/r adapter; parallel Theorems2/4; retained end criterion; core leaf theorem

records.result: For all r≥5 and1≤h≤r−4, literal graph generates S_(2r−1), is string and fails IP.
records.proof: Application Theorem3, explicit tau in P∩Q outside K; group generation; full graph coordinates
records.qualification: Source already proved the disproof; no new question answer.

records.result: Literal two-row family yields S_r wr C2 with IP, every r≥3.
records.proof: Parallel Theorem3; §6 literal source coordinate identification
records.qualification: Uniform proof replaces source finite rank3 check and induction. Abstract group order alone is not the adapter.

records.result: For i≥2 and r=i+1, displayed graph is C with group S_r wr C2.
records.proof: Parallel Theorem3 and §6 adapter n=i+1

records.result: For i≥2 and r>i+1, displayed graph is C with group S_(r+i+1).
records.proof: Parallel Theorem5 first terminal tail, then accepted pure-leaf theorem; §6 adapter
records.qualification: First added edge is proved separately because its predecessor is a compound row swap. No source statement is declared false.

records.result: The unrestricted second gluing proposal fails.
records.proof: Source P4.8 recovered by application Theorem3

records.result: The cited Cameron–Fernandes–Leemans Table6 graph(X) is not always a C-marking.
records.proof: Same literal P4.8 coordinate family
records.qualification: This is the original source’s disproof, not a classification of all other Table6 graphs.

records.result: First small impure endpoint example fails.
records.proof: Accepted core counterexample with explicit S4/S5/D8 subgroup calculation

records.result: Mismatched simplex starts can fail IP.
records.proof: Parallel §2 disconnected deleted set example, explicit pure second-row transposition

records.result: Endpoint sesquiextensions of string C-groups preserve IP.
records.proof: Retained only at application Lemma2
records.qualification: Actual independent central involution and endpoint position checked; original2012 attribution retained.

records.result: End-parabolic C-markings and exact middle intersection imply full IP.
records.proof: Precisely stated application §1, used Lemmas1/2
records.qualification: Classical criterion, not a new common theorem or a complete local proof here.

records.result: Second seven-point impure endpoint example.
records.proof: Application §2, written four-set orbit/end intersection and spanning-transposition path
records.qualification: Same old source example; short explicit derivation supplied during distinct root preliminary review. No new counterexample or finite proof premise.

records.result: Historical sequence1,1,7,9,35,48,135 and any future stability enumeration.
records.proof: Not needed for the source main constructions/disproof
records.qualification: No exhaustive finite-core classification or sequence evaluation is claimed.

records.result: Regular-polytope dictionary, sesquiextension group alternatives, pair-component classification, perfect-split/primitive lemmas.
records.proof: Definitions/context; no use of P2.5/L2.6/T2.7 in the replacement route
records.qualification: Coxeter/polytope correspondence not included in current output; primitive/Jordan inputs removed from actual construction proof, not disproved.
